description:
1st connection. Follow-up to part08-02-driver-bsh, whose bsh tilde test was flawed (advisor review): `echo A=~`/`echo B=~/x` put `~` mid-argument, not at word-start, so POSIX tilde expansion rules never even applied there regardless of shell support - that test proved nothing about bsh's actual leading-tilde behavior. 02-04 (already published on main) tells learners to run `echo 'export PATH=/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin:$PATH' >> ~/.profile` - the `~/.profile` there IS a leading-tilde bare word (outside the quoted echo argument), the exact case that was never actually tested. If bsh does not expand a leading `~`, this command would try to write to a literal path `~/.profile` relative to CWD (a subdirectory literally named `~`), not the learner's real profile - the PATH fix would silently fail to persist across logins even though the current session's two-step export otherwise works. TILDEREDIRECT tests the exact same construct (a leading `~` inside a redirect target) against a disposable scratch filename, never touching the learner's real ~/.profile. TILDEBARE adds advisor's simpler, more direct leading-tilde forms (`echo ~`, `echo ~/x`, `cd ~/vfy && pwd`) as corroborating evidence.

POST-HOC CORRECTION (advisor review of this connection's own results): PRECHECK's own `grep -F '~' </dev/null` was itself broken - the `</dev/null` redirects grep's own stdin, silently discarding the piped `ls -la $HOME` output, so PRECHECK always reported 'none found' regardless of reality. It missed a real, pre-existing `$HOME/~` directory (present since 2026-09-25, likely created by this exact bug during earlier 02-04 testing). TILDEREDIRECT's own diagnostics (`./~`'s `..` entry matches $HOME's own metadata; its contents are only `db`+`vfytilde-scratch.txt`, not $HOME's real contents; `$HOME/vfytilde-scratch.txt` itself was never created) show `$HOME/~` is a real, separate directory - not a symlink back to $HOME - and CLEANUP's `rm -f $HOME/vfytilde-scratch.txt ./~` left `$HOME/~/vfytilde-scratch.txt` behind (it tried to remove the wrong, nonexistent `$HOME/vfytilde-scratch.txt` path, and `rm -f` on a non-empty directory silently no-ops). See docs/probes.md for the corrected account. Not re-run - kept as-is (bug preserved in this description) for an honest record; the next connection that touches $HOME should record `ls -laR "$HOME/~"` before cleaning it up.

steps.label: TILDEREDIRECT
steps.cmd:
cd $HOME
rm -f ./~ 2>&1
rm -rf $HOME/vfytilde-scratch 2>&1
/QOpenSys/usr/bin/bsh -c "echo 'probe line' >> ~/vfytilde-scratch.txt" </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---AFTER-BSH-REDIRECT---
ls -la $HOME/vfytilde-scratch.txt </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---LITERAL-TILDE-CHECK---
ls -la ./~ </dev/null 2>&1
cat ./~ </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---CLEANUP---
rm -f $HOME/vfytilde-scratch.txt ./~ 2>&1
